methodological_rigor.justification: Preclinical platform study (GENEVA) modeling tumor mosaicism and heterogeneous drug responses. Appropriate experimental design using patient-derived xenografts or cell-derived assays to model intratumoral heterogeneity. Statistical analysis of drug response heterogeneity and clonal sensitivity patterns. Limitations acknowledged including model-human concordance uncertainty. Methods appropriate for mechanistic preclinical work.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical platform work addressing important biological problem (tumor mosaicism and drug response heterogeneity). KRAS inhibitor combinations selected based on mechanistic relevance. Translational potential to guide combination therapy design, but clinical validation not demonstrated. Early-stage mechanistic work with limited direct clinical application.

reporting_quality.justification: Preclinical platform methods thoroughly described including tumor model generation, drug testing, and analysis approaches. Sufficient detail for reproducibility. Results presented with appropriate visualizations of clonal heterogeneity and drug response patterns. Limited clinical validation data or biomarker correlation.

novelty_literature.justification: Novel computational/experimental platform (GENEVA) systematically modeling tumor mosaicism and revealing clonal heterogeneity in drug responses. First-of-kind approach to interrogate how intratumoral genetic diversity determines treatment sensitivity and resistance. Identifies potential rational combinations targeting diverse clonal populations.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear presentation of preclinical platform and results. Methods describe model generation and testing approaches. Results show clonal heterogeneity patterns and drug sensitivity variations. Figures effectively display clonal diversity and response heterogeneity. Discussion contextualizes findings within tumor evolution and therapeutic resistance biology.

key_strengths: Novel GENEVA platform systematically models tumor mosaicism and interrogates clonal heterogeneity in drug responses
Identifies distinct clonal drug sensitivities and resistance patterns with potential therapeutic implications
Mechanistic work addressing important biological problem of intratumoral heterogeneity in treatment response
key_concerns: Preclinical platform work without clinical validation; translation to patient benefit speculative
Model-human concordance not directly assessed; results may not reflect clinical drug response heterogeneity
Limited biomarker analysis or mutation-drug response correlations to guide clinical application
KRAS inhibitor combinations mechanistically interesting but clinically validation awaited
chief_reviewer.rationale: Novel preclinical platform with mechanistic insights into tumor heterogeneity and drug response. Appropriate for Tier 3 journals as exploratory mechanistic work with therapeutic potential requiring clinical validation.
